overview: Full audit of example.com — a B2B marketing site. Detected archetype: Marketing / corporate brand. Audit scope tailored accordingly. No Critical findings. Two issues worth addressing: one duplicate canonical that blocks ranking on a key page, one missing OG image that hurts social share CTR.

breakdown.label: Trust signal density
breakdown.note: No visible reviews / testimonials on homepage

top_improvements: Add 3-5 named customer testimonials with LinkedIn attribution — raises Trust signal density from 0/5 to 4/5.
Mention specific partner technologies (AWS, GCP, vendor partnerships) — raises named entities from 11/15 to 14/15.
Add industry-specific terminology (observability, SLA, compliance) to the services section — raises LSI coverage from 16/20 to 19/20.
Add founder/leadership page with photos + credentials + LinkedIn — raises Expertise from 14/20 to 18/20.
Publish 2-3 customer case studies with quantified outcomes — raises Experience from 12/25 to 19/25.
Add 'Press' page collecting mentions in industry publications — raises Authoritativeness from 13/20 to 17/20.

findings.evidence_source: curl -s https://example.com/about | grep -oE '<link rel="canonical"[^>]*>' returns href='https://example.com/' — points to homepage, not self.
findings.section_title: About page canonicalises to homepage — will never rank as a separate page
findings.section_intro: The /about page has <link rel='canonical' href='https://example.com/'> — pointing to the homepage instead of itself. That tells Google the /about URL is a variant of the homepage and shouldn't be indexed as a separate page.
finding_paragraphs: The /about page has a canonical tag pointing to the homepage. Google interprets this as 'this URL is a variant of the homepage — don't index it separately.' Ranking signals from any backlinks to /about flow to the homepage instead.
The result: the /about page cannot rank for queries like 'example about' or 'example team' — Google doesn't index it as a distinct page.
implementation_paragraphs: Set the canonical to the page's own URL. Every page should self-canonical unless it's explicitly a duplicate of another page.
findings.verify: curl -s https://example.com/about | grep -oE '<link rel="canonical"[^>]*>' — href should end with '/about'. Repeat for every non-homepage URL.

findings.evidence_source: curl -s https://example.com/pricing returns no og:image meta tag. Social preview falls back to the platform default image.
findings.section_title: Pricing page has no og:image — social shares show default icon
findings.section_intro: When someone shares the pricing page on LinkedIn / Twitter / WhatsApp, the social preview shows the platform's default image (or no image at all), not a branded card. That hurts CTR on shared links.
finding_paragraphs: The pricing page has no <meta property="og:image"> tag. Social platforms fall back to their default image behavior — typically a generic thumbnail or no preview at all.
For a commercial page where shared links drive conversions, this is a small but consistent CTR drain.
findings.broken_code:
<!-- pricing page <head> — og:image missing -->
<meta property="og:title" content="Pricing | Example">
<meta property="og:description" content="...">
<!-- no og:image -->
implementation_paragraphs: Add og:image + og:image:width + og:image:height + og:image:alt. Use an absolute URL (Facebook/LinkedIn reject relative paths).
findings.fixed_code:
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/images/og/pricing-og.webp">
<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200">
<meta property="og:image:height" content="630">
<meta property="og:image:alt" content="Example pricing plans">
findings.verify: Paste the pricing URL into https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/ — expect a preview with a proper branded image. Repeat on https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/ and https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator.
